data.source_title: Adequacy of Hospital Discharge Summaries in Documenting Tests with Pending Results and Outpatient Follow-up Providers
data.locator: Abstract, Main Results; Methods, pending test sample
data.source_setting: General medicine discharges from two large academic centers in Indianapolis, Indiana
data.source_n: 696 sampled; 668 analyzed; discharge summaries available for 99.2% of 668; 2,927 pending tests
data.quantity: Pending tests mentioned in discharge summaries
data.value: 482/2,927 = 16%; summaries mentioned any pending test in 25%; all tests in 13%
data.unit: tests and percent; discharge summaries and percent
data.source_evidence_basis: The original PubMed abstract returned by NCBI EFetch states 482/2,927 tests (16%) were mentioned; 25% of summaries mentioned any pending tests, 13% all; follow-up provider information was documented in 67% of summaries.
data.limitations: Retrospective random sample at two academic centers; study period and exact summary denominator are not in the inspected abstract. Documentation does not prove completed follow-up or patient notification.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Close discharge by naming pending test, responsible follow-up clinician, expected timing, and escalation/contact plan.
